title: DLMF 26.10 Integer Partitions: Other Restrictions: p\left(\mathcal{D},n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into distinct parts.
summary: DLMF 26.10 Integer Partitions: Other Restrictions: p\left(\mathcal{D},n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into distinct parts.
body: NIST DLMF section 26.10 (Integer Partitions: Other Restrictions) says: "p\left(\mathcal{D},n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into distinct parts. p_{m}\left(\mathcal{D},n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into at most m distinct parts. p\left(\mathcal{D}k,n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into parts with difference at least k . p\left(\mathcal{D}^{\prime}3,n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into parts with difference at least 3, except that multiples of 3 must differ by at least 6. p\left(\mathcal{O},n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into odd parts. p\left(\in\!S,n\right) denotes the number of partitions of n into parts taken from the set S . The set \{n\geq 1\>|\>n\equiv\pm j\ \pmod{k}\} is denoted by A_{j,k} . The set \{2,3,4,\ldots\} is denoted by T . If more than one restriction applies, then the restrictions are separated by commas, for example, p\left(\mathcal{D}2,\hbox{}\!\!\in\!T,n\right) . See Table 26.10.1 ." Equation 26.10.1 on the page has alt text "p\left(\mathcal{D},0\right)=p\left(\mathcal{D}k,0\right)=p\left(\in\!S,0\right% )=1.". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
